review_candidates.title: Analista de negócios da cadeia de suprimentos
review_candidates.description: SUMMARY The COGS Control & Automation Analyst is responsible for the integrity of the company’s cost of goods sold across all restaurant locations (Fort Lauderdale, Charlotte, Washington DC and Orlando). The role owns three pillars: automating vendor invoice entry so that manual handling is limited to exceptions; maintaining the COGS item database (items, unit conversions, vendor-item links and recipes) across purchasing, inventory and point-of-sale systems; and monitoring the purchases made by restaurant managers against approved vendors, order guides and contract pricing, supported by the NextEdge price-comparison platform. The position requires deep familiarity with accounting and purchasing software (Restaurant 365), point-of-sale systems (Toast) and process automation tools. The COGS Control & Automation Analyst reports directly to the Controller and works closely with the General Managers, the Operations Manager, the BI Analyst and vendors. Rather than negotiating and purchasing, this role ensures that every dollar purchased by the restaurants is recorded correctly, at the right price, and accurately reflected in food cost. This is a systems- and data-driven, high-accountability position and the sole owner of the cost-control function. DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES Implement and maintain automated invoice capture (OCR, EDI integrations and vendor portals) in Restaurant 365 or the company’s AP system. Configure and maintain vendor-item mapping, unit-of-measure conversions and GL coding rules so that invoices post without manual entry. Manage the daily invoice exception queue (unrecognized items, price or quantity variances, missing invoices) and eliminate the root cause of recurring exceptions. Track and report monthly the percentage of invoices processed without manual entry, continuously reducing manual handling. Own the COGS item database: create, update and deactivate items across purchasing, inventory and POS systems. Maintain recipes linked to Toast menu items so that theoretical food cost is reliable. Ensure a consistent item structure and categories across inventory counts, recipes and purchases. Keep NextEdge updated with items, approved vendors and contract prices. Build and maintain order guides for each restaurant with approved vendors and items. Identify and recommend vendor or item substitution opportunities based on price comparisons. Monitor purchases weekly by location: price paid vs. contract and NextEdge pricing, off-guide or non-approved vendor purchases, and volume purchased vs. sales. Closely monitor meat purchases (approximately 70% of food cost): price per pound, yield and consumption per guest served. Calculate theoretical vs. actual food cost variance at every period close and investigate the largest variances with General Managers. Issue alerts and periodic COGS reports to the Controller and General Managers. Support period-end inventory counts and the analysis of count discrepancies.
